title: Blitz question pack
description: The structured index of one book. See docs/question-pack-schema.md for the prose version. Validate with `blitz import-pack <file> --dry-run`, which checks everything this schema does plus the things a schema cannot: that dot point ids exist in the current study design, that the fingerprint is current, that bboxes fall inside the source PDF, that figure files exist, and that depends_on resolves.

pack_version.description: Schema version. Major version must match the importer's.

subject_id.description: Must match a study design installed in Blitz.

study_design_fingerprint.description: From `blitz dot-points <subject> --json`. Dot point ids are positional, so a study design re-import can leave every id valid while changing what it means. A mismatch is a hard error. Omitting it is allowed but warns.

status.description: Default review state for every question in the pack. Per-question status overrides it.
Anything other than 'approved' lands unverified in the index.

id.description: Stable across re-imports; re-importing updates rows in place rather than duplicating them. Also namespaces question ids and depends_on ids.

title.description: Printed in the citation under every question.

pdf.description: Path to the source PDF on the machine running the import. Required if any figure uses page/bbox. Never copied into the repo.

page_offset.description: Printed page number minus PDF page index. Only used when a question has no printed_page of its own.

id.description: Unique within the pack, stable across re-runs. Stored as '<source.id>-<id>'.

title.description: Short human label, shown in listings and review tools. Not printed on sheets.

provenance.description: Printed in the citation, in square brackets.

printed_page.description: The page number AS PRINTED IN THE BOOK, not the PDF index. String because books use roman numerals and suffixes.

source_number.description: The question number as printed in the book.

kk_ids.description: Study design dot points this question assesses, best first. Must exist in the current study design. Taken as given — the tagger is not consulted for pack rows. An empty list imports the question but counts it untagged, so it can never be selected.

question_type.description: An id from the subject's question_types. See `blitz dot-points <subject> --json`.

marks.description: Total marks. If omitted, summed from parts[].marks.

difficulty.description: 1 recall .. 5 hardest exam standard. Omit rather than guess; the picker treats it as unknown.

stem.description: The question, or the shared lead-in to its parts. Real Unicode notation: 'm s⁻²', not 'm s-2'.

parts.description: Sub-parts. Printed on their own lines with their own ruled answer space.

options.description: Multiple choice options in order, WITHOUT the leading 'A ' / 'B ' — Blitz relabels them.

answer.description: The worked solution. OMIT ENTIRELY where the book supplies none — do not generate one. Blitz prints 'no worked solution in the source' with the citation.

context.description: The scenario this question is set in, printed above it in the book. Stored separately from stem and printed above the question, so a question never reaches a sheet without what it is about. Repeat it on each question in a shared run.

depends_on.description: Ids of questions IN THIS PACK that must accompany this one (e.g. 'using your answer from the previous question'). Unnamespaced — Blitz prefixes them with source.id. Ids that do not resolve within the pack are a validation error. The picker pulls prerequisites onto the sheet ahead of the question that needs them.

figures.description: Every figure this question needs, IN ORDER. A question routinely needs several: a page continuation, the shared scenario above it, or an earlier question it depends on. All 'question' figures are stacked into the question and all 'answer' figures into the solution.

render_mode.description: 'crop' means the text could not be faithfully reconstructed (stacked fractions, equation-editor glyphs), so Blitz prints the page image and uses the text only for search and tagging. Requires at least one 'question' figure.

answer_mode.description: As render_mode, for the worked solution. Judge it independently: solutions are where the algebra lives, so they need cropping far more often than questions do. Requires at least one 'answer' figure.

review.description: What still needs a human on this question. Any entry makes the row unverified.

notes.description: Editorial record: why an answer is missing, what wording was changed, why a crop was used. Kept with the row and shown when reviewing the index.

page.description: 0-BASED page index in source.pdf. Must be within the document.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF points, origin TOP-LEFT of the page. x0<x1 and y0<y1. Crop to the content, not the whole page: a crop wider than about 400pt forces the sheet into a single column to stay legible.

file.description: Path to an image, relative to the pack file. Alternative to page+bbox.

caption.description: Printed under the figure when a question has more than one.
